findings.title: Unhealthy flusher process is never killed (isinstance check is always False for spawn processes)
findings.body: `_ensure_processes_alive()` only kills the old process if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. The processes here are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, i.e. `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which is **not** a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process` (`multiprocessing.context.Process`) — both derive separately from `BaseProcess`. So the check is always False and `process.kill()` never runs, whereas the previous code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. Consequences: a hung-but-alive flusher process is left running while a replacement is spawned for the same shards, so two processes flush the same Redis shards concurrently (duplicate segments produced to `buffered-segments`, racing `done_flush_segments`), and the zombie keeps writing to the shared `process_healthy_since` Value, permanently masking hang detection and leaking a process on every restart. The same wrong check also makes `process.terminate()` in `join()` (line 346) a no-op. Use `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` (or `self.mp_context.Process`) in the isinstance check.

findings.title: max_processes=None/0 silently means one process per shard
findings.body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means that any caller that does not pass `max_processes` (the default, used by every direct construction such as `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py`) spawns one OS process per assigned shard, while the CLI option `--flusher-processes` defaults to 1. A consumer assigned 32 partitions constructed without the option would fork 32 flusher processes, each with its own Redis connections — a large, unintended resource jump compared to the previous single-process behaviour. Additionally, because of `or`, an explicit `--flusher-processes 0` is silently reinterpreted as "one per shard" instead of being rejected. Make the default explicit (e.g. 1) and validate that the value is >= 1.

findings.title: join() can skip terminating remaining processes and computes an unused variable
findings.body: In `join()`, `remaining_time` is computed but never used, and when the deadline has passed the loop `break`s, so the remaining processes in `self.processes` are never waited for nor terminated (they are only daemonic, so they are killed when the parent exits, possibly mid-flush). Combined with the broken `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check on line 346, no spawn process is ever terminated at shutdown. Either drop the unused variable and terminate all processes regardless of deadline, or document why skipping is acceptable.

findings.title: Dead method `_create_process_for_shard`
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(shard)` is not called anywhere after the refactor (restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`). Leaving it in is confusing because it looks like the per-shard restart path but would silently do nothing if `shard` is not in any mapping. Remove it.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: "shards" vs "shard"
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `{"shards": shard_tag}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `{"shard": shard_tag}`. Queries/dashboards grouping on a single tag name will silently miss one of these metrics. Pick one key.

findings.title: Comma-joined shard list used as metric tag value creates unbounded cardinality
findings.body: `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` is used as the `shard` tag on `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and the per-segment `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` timing. The value is a *set* of shards that changes with every Kafka rebalance and with the `--flusher-processes` setting, so the tag value space is combinatorial rather than bounded by the number of shards, and `segment_size_bytes` is emitted per segment. This can blow up metric cardinality and makes per-shard aggregation impossible. Consider tagging with the process index or omitting the tag on high-volume metrics.

findings.title: Class docstring contradicts actual process allocation and omits max_processes
findings.body: The docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but shards are actually bucketed round-robin into `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` processes, and the CLI default is a single process for all shards. The docstring also still documents a `:param topic:` that does not exist while the newly added `max_processes` parameter is undocumented.

findings.title: Added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: Line 15 does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, so the `time.sleep(0.1)` added at line 62 ("Give flusher threads time to process after drift change") returns immediately and provides no synchronization at all. The test still relies on the flusher thread happening to flush before `step.join()` sets the stop flag, so it remains racy/flaky and the comment is misleading. Use a real wait (e.g. `monkeypatch`-free sleep, or poll `messages` with a timeout) instead.

findings.title: Shard-distribution assertion cannot detect duplicated or missing shards
findings.body: `total_shards = sum(len(shards) for shards in flusher.process_to_shards_map.values()); assert total_shards == 4` would also pass if the same shard were assigned to two processes while another shard was dropped entirely — exactly the kind of bug that would cause duplicate or lost segments. Assert on the union instead, e.g. that the concatenation of all lists equals `{0,1,2,3}` with no duplicates, and that the buckets are balanced.

findings.title: No test exercises the multiprocess flusher path
findings.body: Both new/updated tests pass `produce_to_pipe`, which makes `SpanFlusher` use `threading.Thread` instead of `mp_context.Process`. The core change of this PR — spawning a real process per shard group, pickling a per-shard `SpansBuffer` into it, restarting a dead/hung process, and the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` kill/terminate paths — is therefore completely untested (and indeed broken, see the isinstance finding). Add at least one test that drives the actual spawn-process path, or a unit test of `_ensure_processes_alive` with a fake spawn process.
